questions.q: What is the maximum pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum under the Consumer Protection Act 1986?
questions.a: The District Forum can entertain complaints where the value of goods/services and compensation claimed does not exceed ₹20 lakh. A wrong answer (e.g., ₹1 crore or no limit) reveals confusion between the three tiers' monetary limits — a frequent board exam error where students swap District and State Commission limits.

questions.q: Explain why the Consumer Protection Act 1986 created a three-tier redressal system instead of a single national forum.
questions.a: The three-tier system ensures access to justice at the local level (District Forum), reduces burden on higher forums, and provides an appeal hierarchy. A wrong answer focusing only on "speed" or "cost" misses the structural reasoning: decentralisation for accessibility, graded jurisdiction by claim value, and appellate review — all three are needed for full marks.

questions.q: A consumer in Delhi buys a laptop worth ₹25 lakh that malfunctions. The seller refuses repair. Which forum should the consumer approach first, and what is the time limit to appeal if dissatisfied?
questions.a: The consumer must file in the State Commission (Delhi) because the claim exceeds ₹20 lakh but is within ₹1 crore. Appeal to the National Commission must be filed within 30 days of the State Commission's order. A wrong forum choice (District Forum) shows misunderstanding of pecuniary jurisdiction; missing the 30-day limit indicates ignorance of procedural deadlines.

questions.q: Compare the composition of the District Forum and the National Commission. Why does the National Commission have more members?
questions.a: District Forum: President (qualified as District Judge) + 2 members (one woman). National Commission: President (Supreme Court judge/retired) + 4+ members (one woman). The National Commission handles higher-value, complex cases and appeals, requiring broader expertise and quorum for bench decisions. A wrong answer stating identical composition ignores the Act's scaling of judicial capacity with case gravity.

questions.q: "Under the 1986 Act, a consumer can directly approach the National Commission for a claim of ₹5 lakh." Evaluate this statement.
questions.a: False. The National Commission's original jurisdiction starts at ₹1 crore. A ₹5 lakh claim must begin at the District Forum. Direct filing at a higher forum is not permitted — the Act mandates the ladder based on claim value. This tests whether the student understands that jurisdiction is mandatory, not optional.

questions.q: Design a flowchart showing the path of a consumer complaint from filing to final appeal under the 1986 Act, including pecuniary thresholds and appeal time limits.
questions.a: A good flowchart has three boxes: District Forum (≤₹20 lakh) → appeal in 30 days → State Commission (₹20 lakh–₹1 crore) → appeal in 30 days → National Commission (>₹1 crore) → appeal to Supreme Court in 30 days. Missing thresholds, wrong time limits, or skipping the Supreme Court appeal indicates incomplete mental model of the hierarchy.
